overall_reason: The product is specific (a CLI design database with real counts and a worked pet-grooming prompt), but the page itself is the dark SaaS template it sells: gradient accent word on every h2, six-tile stat band, equal icon-tile glass cards, 'Everything You Need for Beautiful UI', numbered how-it-works steps, partner logo grid and a 'Ready to Build' CTA band.

findings.evidence: T-STOCK-ORDER: hero with tool-logo chip row and two CTAs > 6-tile stat band (57 / 95 / 56 / 8 / 24 / 29) > 'Everything You Need for Beautiful UI' 3x2 equal icon cards > 'Supported' stack grid (8 equal cards) > 'How It Works' 1-to-6 numbered steps > gallery grid with filter chips > partner logo grid ('Other') > 'Build with Us' 3 icon cards + CTA panel > 'Ready to Build' CTA band > link-farm footer. Nine stock sections in stock order: generated by the skill's own rule even though the copy is specific.
findings.before: stat band > feature cards > stack grid > 1-2-3 steps > gallery > logos > icon cards > CTA > CTA
findings.after: Lead with the worked example (prompt > reasoning > database hits > result) as the hero, since it is the one thing only this product can show; cut the second CTA panel and the 'Build with Us' cross-promotion
findings.why: Specific words on a default skeleton still read as a default page.

findings.evidence: Blue #2563eb to orange #f97316 gradient on the last word of each heading: 'UI UX Pro Max', 'Beautiful UI', 'How It Works', 'Build with Us', and others (18 gradient hits in sweep). The h2s are split so the gradient word sits in a separate span ('Supported' + gradient, 'How It' + gradient).
findings.before: Everything You Need for Beautiful UI
findings.after: Plain headings; reserve the gradient for the wordmark only
findings.why: Accented-word gradient on every heading is a top AI-landing reflex (SLP-163).

findings.evidence: saas-card-kit and violet-gradient clusters (sweep) confirmed by eye: navy-black ground with blue and orange radial glows behind the hero (tile 1440-00), translucent glass cards with 1px borders on every section, tinted icon tiles above every card heading (Design Styles, Color Palettes, High-Trust Verification...), Tailwind default swatches as tokens (#3b82f6, #1e293b, #f8fafc). Failed T-MIRROR: any AI dev-tool landing would get this hero, card grid and CTA band.
findings.before: Glass card kit + radial glows + Tailwind slate
findings.after: Show the database itself (a real slice of the styles table, a palette row, a font pairing set in its fonts) instead of describing it in icon cards
findings.why: A design-intelligence product that renders as the default look undermines its own claim.

findings.evidence: Six equal glass tiles with icon + big blue number + label: '57 UI Styles', '95 Color Palettes', '56 Font Pairings', '8 Tech Stacks', '24 Chart Types', '29 Landing Patterns'. The feature card below then says '45+ more styles' and '50+ font pairings' and the Landing Patterns card says '14 conversion-optimized page structures', contradicting 29.
findings.after: One source of truth for counts; drop the stat band or reduce to one line under the install command
findings.why: A stat band is a stock hero accessory; inconsistent figures make it read as filler (T-THREE-LINE: falsifiable and failing).

findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: 'Comprehensive design intelligence at your fingertips. Search, discover, and implement stunning interfaces with AI-powered recommendations.', 'Everything You Need for Beautiful UI', 'From prompt to production-ready UI in 6 intelligent steps', 'Ready to showcase your product to real builders?'. Sweep lexicon also caught 'supercharge'.
findings.after: "57 styles, 95 palettes and 56 font pairings your coding agent can search from the CLI."
findings.why: Stock phrases in headings and sub-lines fit any tool.

findings.where: 'From Our Team' pill and final CTA band
findings.evidence: Rocket emoji used as decoration twice: '🚀 From Our Team' eyebrow pill (tile 1440-06 bottom) and a 60px '🚀' above the closing CTA (sweep SLP-010). Small coloured pill eyebrows recur ('Open for Launches', 'From Our Team').
findings.after: Delete the emoji and the pill; the heading 'Other Products' is enough
findings.why: Emoji as heading decoration is a template tell.

strengths: The 'How It Works' walk-through uses a concrete prompt ('Build a landing page for a pet grooming service...') and shows the actual database hits (Fredoka + Nunito, 'Use animations for loading only'): specific and only-this-product.
The install line '$ uipro init --ai claude' in the hero tells developers exactly what to do.
not_investigated: gallery thumbnails rendered as empty dark boxes in tiles (lazy images loaded after the screenshot; alt and src are present in dom-1440.json), so the demo imagery was not judged
